subject: Data residency & default retention — clarifying what Redwood stores by default
messages:
From: Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@acmehealth.com, security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: where request/response data lives and how long you keep prompts/outputs

Hi Lauren,

We're reviewing Redwood for a pilot and have a couple of specific questions we need to document for our security review:

1) By default, when we call the hosted API from our US region, does Redwood store the raw request (prompt) and the generated response? If so, where (region/namespace) is that stored?

2) What’s the default retention period for request/response pairs, and for derived artifacts (embeddings, rerank inputs)?

3) Is there an automated deletion path we can call (API or support ticket) that removes our customer data earlier than the default TTL? What evidence do you provide after deletion (audit id, snapshot)?

4) Any exceptions — telemetry, system logs, or debugging snapshots — that persist beyond the retention window we should be aware of?

We attached our internal checklist (Acme_SSP_v3.pdf). Appreciate a concise, authoritative answer we can include in the checklist.

Thanks,
Sam
Security Engineer — Acme Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Samuel Kim <samuel.kim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where request/response data lives and how long you keep prompts/outputs

Hi Sam, Lauren — answering each question succinctly (and calling out a couple of important edge cases):

1) Default storage and residency:
- Hosted API: By default, request payloads (prompts) and generated outputs are ingested into our short-term inference store and persisted in the same geographic region where the request was served (in your case, US-east or US-west depending on endpoint routing). That store is isolated per-customer namespace for auditability.
- Note: Private/Dedicated deployments behave differently (data stays on your VPC or dedicated pool; nothing leaves your environment unless you opt into Redwood-managed telemetry).

2) Default retention windows (hosted):
- Request/response pairs (prompts + generated outputs): default TTL = 30 days.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, rerank indexes created by Redwood): default TTL = 90 days.
- Aggregated telemetry (metrics/latency buckets): retained 13 months at an aggregated level; low-cardinality request traces are purged faster (default 90 days).

3) Early deletion and evidence:
- Self-service deletion: We offer an API endpoint for customers to request expedited purge of stored request/response pairs within their namespace. Endpoint: POST /v1/customers/{id}/purge-requests (support-enforced, non-reversible).
- Support-assisted deletion: we can also execute on your behalf and provide an immutable deletion certificate containing: deletion request id, affected namespaces, time range, S3 object ids removed (or internal shard ids), and a signed timestamp from our key management service.
- Note on backups: Backups/snapshots used for disaster recovery are rotated and respect tenancy boundaries; we maintain a separate backup retention policy (default 90 days) and can exclude your tenant from backup retention on enterprise contracts.

4) Exceptions and debugging artifacts:
- System telemetry (service health metrics) is aggregated and non-identifying; it does not contain full prompt/response text.
- Debugging traces and sampling: In rare cases where an automated trace needs to capture a request payload for troubleshooting, that data is flagged and retained for investigation for up to 180 days and is strictly access controlled. We provide customers the option to opt out of captured payloads in our support portal; high-severity incidents may require temporary capture with customer consent.

Extra clarity: Prompts vs outputs and what 'counts' as user data:
- "Prompt" = the raw request body you send (including system user messages and tool instructions).
- "Output" = model-generated tokens returned by Redwood. Both are treated as customer data and fall under the TTL above unless you enable the opt-out.

If you need, we can prepare a signed statement for your compliance file that lists the default TTLs, the API URL for purge, and the format of the deletion certificate.

— Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — very helpful. A few quick follow-ups so we can finish the checklist:

- For the 30-day TTL on request/response pairs: is that configurable per-customer? E.g., can we have a 7-day default for our pilot?
- For the backup exclusion: what contract language or admin action is required to exclude our tenant from backups?
- For deletion evidence — can you provide a sample deletion certificate we can redact and store in our audit binder?

Also, one more ask: we run a small batch of embeddings for PII redaction upstream. Do embeddings count as outputs for TTL? You mentioned derived artifacts at 90 days — does that include embeddings produced by our calls?

Appreciate it,
Sam

Sam, quick follow-up with commitments and next steps:

- Configurable TTLs: Yes — for hosted customers we support adjusted retention policies as part of an enterprise pilot. For your pilot we can set request/response TTL to 7 days and embedding TTL to 30 days. I will file a pilot change request and Rishi will include the change in the deletion certificate format.
- Backup exclusion: This requires an addendum to the contract (we'll add a short clause for backup exclusion and provide operational instructions). Our Customer Success rep will prepare the addendum.
- Sample deletion certificate: Attached is a redacted example (redwood-dataflow-diagram.png demonstrates namespace boundaries; Acme_SSP_v3.pdf is your checklist). We'll also put a template of the certificate into the support ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/56821

Next steps: I'll schedule a 30-minute technical review next week to walk your security and devops through the purge API and the certificate fields. Proposed times: Tue 06/26 between 10–12 PT or Wed 06/27 afternoon PT. Please share availability.

Thanks — talk soon.
